standard_text: Simple machines (lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge, screw) make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 5, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 5 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): pulleys, gears, levers and other machines, work and energy and mechanical advantage. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Simple machines change the size or direction of a force.
key_sub: Less force over a longer distance.
body_html:
How to think about it

The six simple machines are the lever, wedge, inclined plane, wheel and axle, pulley and screw. They make work easier by changing the size or direction of a force: a ramp lets you use less force over a longer distance.

Compound machines, like a bicycle, combine simple machines. Your arm is a natural lever. Power is how fast energy is transferred: a more powerful motor does the same work in less time.

Example

Which simple machine is a ramp?

A sloping surface

Answer: an inclined plane

Example

A single fixed pulley on a flagpole: what does it change?

You pull down, the flag goes up.

Answer: the direction of the force

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a machine reduces the work done (it reduces the force).
  • Mixing up a wedge and an inclined plane.
  • Thinking power and force are the same.

faq.q: Why is a door handle far from the hinges?
faq.a: A longer lever arm needs less force to turn the door.
The rate of transferring energy, measured in watts.

items.q: What is a pulley?
c: a wheel with a groove that a rope runs over
a flat board on a pivot
items.e: Pulleys help lift loads.

items.q: In a pulley system, why does the effort get smaller with more ropes?
c: The load is shared between the ropes.
items.e: But you pull more rope.

items.q: On a bike, what links the pedal gear to the back-wheel gear?
items.e: Gears linked by a chain turn the same way.

items.q: What happens when two gears touch and one turns?
c: The other turns the same way.
The other turns the opposite way.
items.e: Teeth push each other.

items.q: A small gear with 10 teeth drives a big gear with 30 teeth. How do they compare?
c: The big gear turns more slowly.
The big gear turns backward and faster.
Both turn at the same speed.
items.e: The small gear turns 3 times for each turn of the big gear.

items.q: Why do people oil the gears of a bike?
c: to reduce friction so they turn easily
items.e: Less friction, less wear.

items.q: Which pair of gears would turn the slowest output gear?
items.e: The bigger the driven gear compared with the driver, the slower it turns.

items.q: Which machine changes a small turning force at the handle into a big force at the axle?
c: a wheel and axle, like a doorknob
items.e: The big wheel makes turning easier.

items.q: 3 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear C turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 3 gears, gear C turns clockwise.

items.q: Why does a big gear driven by a small gear turn more slowly?
c: It has more teeth, so the small gear must turn more times for one big turn.
Gears always turn at the same speed.
items.e: Count the teeth.

items.q: Which simple machine is made of a rope over a grooved wheel?
items.e: That is the definition of a pulley.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a hand-held egg whisk?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: What is a mechanism?
c: a set of moving parts that work together to do a job
items.e: Gears, pulleys and levers can make mechanisms.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 90-tooth gear. The big gear turns 3 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 90 teeth, which is 3 turns of the small gear. 3 × 3 = 9.

items.q: A water well has a crank and a rope around a drum. Which machine is this?
items.e: Turning the crank winds the rope.

items.q: What is the effort in a pulley system?
items.e: Effort is the force that makes the machine work.

items.q: 2 gears are meshed in a row: A → B. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 2 gears, gear B turns anticlockwise.

items.q: Which tool uses a pulley to lift heavy car engines in a garage?
items.e: Chain blocks use several pulleys.

items.q: Why is it easier to open a paint can with a long screwdriver than with a coin?
c: The longer lever needs less effort.
items.e: A longer lever arm means less effort.

items.q: What does a single fixed pulley do?
c: changes the direction of the force, so you pull down to lift up
items.e: Flagpoles use this.

items.q: 4 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D. Gear A turns anticlockwise. Which way does gear D turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 4 gears, gear D turns clockwise.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 90-tooth gear. The small gear turns 3 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: A 10-tooth gear drives a 20-tooth gear. The small gear turns 6 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 2 times as many teeth, so it turns 2 times more slowly. 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

items.q: A small gear with 20 teeth drives a big gear with 80 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 2 times?
items.e: 80 ÷ 20 = 4 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: A small gear with 12 teeth drives a big gear with 24 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 6 times?
items.e: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: 4 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear D turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 4 gears, gear D turns anticlockwise.

items.q: 2 gears are meshed in a row: A → B. Gear A turns anticlockwise. Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 2 gears, gear B turns clockwise.

items.q: To make a seesaw balance with a heavier child, where should the heavier child sit?
items.e: Moving closer reduces their turning effect.

items.q: Gear A (15 teeth) turns clockwise and drives gear B (30 teeth). Which way does gear B turn?
items.e: Two gears that touch turn in opposite directions.

items.q: A small gear with 15 teeth drives a big gear with 45 teeth. The small gear turns 6 times. How many times does the big gear turn?

items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 3 gears, gear C turns anticlockwise.

items.q: 5 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D → E. Gear A turns clockwise. Which way does gear E turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 5 gears, gear E turns clockwise.

items.q: Which design makes the effort smaller in a pulley system?
c: tying the rope to the load only
using more pulleys and more rope sections to hold the load
items.e: More supporting ropes share the load.

items.q: A 30-tooth gear drives a 120-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 120 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 1 × 4 = 4.

items.q: 5 gears are meshed in a row: A → B → C → D → E. Gear A turns anticlockwise. Which way does gear E turn?
items.e: Each meshed gear turns the opposite way to the one before it. With 5 gears, gear E turns anticlockwise.

items.q: A 24-tooth gear drives a 96-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 96 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 1 × 4 = 4.

items.q: A 24-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The small gear turns 4 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 2 times as many teeth, so it turns 2 times more slowly. 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

items.q: How can you make a lever lift a load with less effort?
items.e: Longer distance, less force.

items.q: A small gear with 8 teeth drives a big gear with 32 teeth. How many times does the small gear turn while the big gear turns 6 times?
items.e: 32 ÷ 8 = 4 small turns for each big turn.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in scissors?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a crowbar?

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The small gear turns 9 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 3 times as many teeth, so it turns 3 times more slowly. 9 ÷ 3 = 3.

items.q: A lever has a pivot, a load and an effort. Which part does a lever turn around?
items.e: The pivot is the turning point.

items.q: Why does an elevator use a motor and pulleys?
c: to lift heavy loads with less effort
items.e: Machines make work easier.

items.q: Why do conveyor belts in a factory use pulleys?
c: the belt runs over pulleys that keep it moving
items.e: Belts and pulleys move objects.

items.q: Which design would make a model crane lift a heavier load?
c: add a second pulley to share the load
make the arm out of paper
items.e: More pulleys reduce the force needed.

items.q: A 15-tooth gear drives a 30-tooth gear. The small gear turns 4 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 2 times as many teeth, so it turns 2 times more slowly. 4 ÷ 2 = 2.

items.q: A 12-tooth gear drives a 48-tooth gear. The big gear turns 1 time. How many times does the small gear turn?

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 64-tooth gear. The big gear turns 2 times. How many times does the small gear turn?
items.e: Each turn of the big gear moves 64 teeth, which is 4 turns of the small gear. 2 × 4 = 8.

items.q: Which is an example of a pulley in daily life?
c: window blinds pulled up with a cord
items.e: The cord runs over small pulleys.

items.q: What is a load in a machine?
c: the object being moved or lifted
items.e: The effort moves the load.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in window blinds?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Why do car engines use belts and pulleys?
c: to turn other parts, like the fan, with the engine's motion
items.e: Belts carry motion between pulleys.

items.q: Two gears are meshed. The first turns clockwise. Which way does the second turn?

items.q: Which mechanism changes turning motion into up-and-down motion in a toy?
items.e: Cams are used in moving toys.

items.q: A 16-tooth gear drives a 64-tooth gear. The small gear turns 8 times. How many times does the big gear turn?
items.e: The big gear has 4 times as many teeth, so it turns 4 times more slowly. 8 ÷ 4 = 2.

items.q: What kind of mechanism is used in a wheelbarrow?
items.e: Levers, pulleys and gears are simple machines.

items.q: Why do cranes use several pulleys together?
c: so a smaller force can lift a heavy load
items.e: More pulleys share the load, but you pull more rope.

A lever lifts a load of 320 N with an effort of 40 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
items.e: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 320 ÷ 40 = 8.

items.q: A light bulb receives 50 J of electrical energy and gives out 30 J of light energy. How much energy is converted to thermal energy?
items.e: Total energy out = total energy in: 50 − 30 = 20 J.

items.q: A student pushes a box with a force of 150 N for 5 m. How much work is done?
items.e: Work = force × distance = 150 N × 5 m = 750 J.

items.q: A ball has 200 J of gravitational potential energy at the top of a fall. Ignoring air resistance, how much kinetic energy does it have just before it hits the ground?
items.e: Energy is conserved: all the potential energy becomes kinetic energy.

items.q: Which is an environmental cost of a transportation system?

items.e: Public transit can reduce the cost.

items.q: Chioma does 30 J of work moving a load with a force of 20 N. How far does the load move?
items.e: distance = work ÷ force = 30 ÷ 20.

items.e: work done = force × distance = 20 × 4 = 80 J.

items.q: A ball dropped with 100 J of potential energy bounces back up with 75 J. Where did the rest of the energy go?
c: It was stored in the ground forever as potential energy.
It was converted to thermal and sound energy.
It became new mass in the ball.
items.e: Energy is not destroyed: 25 J is converted to thermal and sound energy.

items.q: A machine uses 200 J of energy (work in) and does 160 J of useful work (work out). What is its efficiency?
items.e: Efficiency = work out ÷ work in × 100% = 160 ÷ 200 × 100% = 80%.

items.q: Blessing pulls a sledge with a force of 10 N for 5 m. How much work is done?

items.q: What is the output of a system?

items.q: Which simple machine is a screw?

items.q: Obinna (weight 500 N) sits 1 m from the pivot of a see-saw. Abdullahi weighs 400 N. How far from the pivot on the other side must Abdullahi sit to balance it?
items.e: Balanced: 500 × 1 = 400 × d, so d = 1.25 m. The lighter person sits further away.
